elements.element: Customer owns Deliverables and work product created for Customer.
elements.evidence: 14.2 (untouched): "Upon creation and subject to payment of the applicable Fees, Customer owns each Deliverable created specifically for Customer." Deliverable is defined in 1.4 to cover reports, configurations, designs and "other work product" identified in an Order Form as created specifically for Customer.

elements.element: Vendor assigns the Deliverables and work product to Customer.
elements.evidence: 14.2: "Vendor hereby assigns to Customer all worldwide right, title, and interest in those Deliverables and shall obtain equivalent assignments from its personnel." Present-tense assignment plus further-assurances sentence.

elements.element: Vendor retains its pre-existing intellectual property.
elements.evidence: 14.3: "Vendor retains Vendor Technology." Definition 1.9 confines Vendor Technology to Vendor's pre-existing software, tools, models, templates and modifications that are not Deliverables and exclude Customer Data and pre-Effective-Date Customer IP.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Vendor IP embedded in Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: 13.2: for Vendor Technology "embedded in a Deliverable, Vendor grants Customer and its Affiliates a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid licence"; 14.3 cross-refers ("the perpetual licence in Section 13.2 applies") and the cross-reference survives unedited.

elements.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: 13.2 expressly states the licence is "irrevocable" and "fully paid"; no retained sentence conditions or revokes it.

elements.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: 13.2: "royalty-free, fully paid licence" to use, modify, create derivative works and permit contractors to support the material for Customer's business.

elements.element: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data.
elements.evidence: 14.1 first sentence retained: "As between the Parties, Customer owns all Customer Data, Customer Confidential Information, Customer-provided material, and intellectual property Customer owned or developed independently of the Services." No assignment of Customer Data or Customer IP to Vendor remains anywhere in the rendered text.

elements.element: Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.
elements.evidence: As redlined, 14.1 second sentence reads "No right transfers to Vendor except the limited right to process that material solely to provide the Services for Customer" (the "secure, support, and improve" expansion is gone), and 15.1 reads "Vendor shall process Customer Data only on Customer's documented instructions and solely to provide the Services" with the "as permitted by this Agreement" hook and the consent-based model-training carve-out removed, so no broader exploitation, improvement or consent-gated training right survives.

elements.element: The parties do not jointly own intellectual property.
elements.evidence: 14.4 retained: "No jointly owned intellectual property is created unless the Parties sign a separate instrument identifying it and their exploitation rights." The default is no joint ownership; the exception requires a future signed instrument that would itself define exploitation rights, so no joint ownership arises under this Agreement.

elements.element: Vendor may retain ownership of generic tools and know-how.
elements.evidence: 14.3 "Vendor retains Vendor Technology" (1.9: pre-existing software, tools, models, templates, routines, connectors) and 1.4 excludes from Deliverables "generally applicable ideas, methods, skills, and know-how retained in the unaided memory of Vendor personnel."

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: Satisfied a fortiori: Customer owns the Deliverables outright under 14.2 with a present assignment, and any embedded Vendor Technology needed to use them carries the perpetual licence in 13.2.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: Ownership under 14.2 is not revocable, and the 13.2 licence to embedded Vendor Technology is expressly "irrevocable"; no retained clause permits Vendor to terminate Customer's rights in Deliverables.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is worldwide.
elements.evidence: 14.2 assigns "all worldwide right, title, and interest" in the Deliverables; 13.2 grants a "worldwide" licence to embedded Vendor Technology.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: No further royalty attaches: 14.2 vests ownership subject only to payment of the applicable Fees, and 13.2 is "royalty-free, fully paid."

elements.element: Customer may use and modify Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: Ownership under 14.2 permits use and modification; 13.2 expressly allows Customer and its Affiliates to "use, execute, reproduce, display, perform, modify, create derivative works from" embedded Vendor Technology "for Customer's business," and 14.3 bars third-party material that materially restricts Customer's intended use without approval.

elements.element: Customer may sublicense Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: As assignee-owner of the Deliverables (14.2) Customer may sublicense them; 13.2 additionally extends to Affiliates and permits contractors to support the embedded material. No retained restriction on Customer's onward grant of Deliverables appears in the rendered text.

elements.element: Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.
elements.evidence: Same operative language as at the preferred level: redlined 14.1 ("solely to provide the Services for Customer") and 15.1 ("only on Customer's documented instructions and solely to provide the Services"), with the improvement, agreement-wide and consent-based training expansions deleted.

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: ownership (14.2), assignment (14.2), retained Vendor pre-existing IP (14.3/1.9), the perpetual-irrevocable-royalty-free embedded-IP licence (13.2), Customer Data ownership (14.1) and no joint ownership (14.4) were already met, and the single failing element — the scope of Vendor's rights in Customer Data — is now cured in operative language rather than merely promised in the comment.

The three deletions are all inside the single target element. Removing "improve the Services" from 14.1, "and as permitted by this Agreement" from 15.1, and the "without Customer's express written consent" carve-out from the model-training prohibition are each required: an improvement right, an agreement-wide hook, and a consent-gated training right all defeat "solely to provide the Services" under the applicable rule boundary.

Dropping "secure, support" from 14.1 alongside "improve" does not exceed the element or lose favourable language: the element demands the exact "solely to provide the Services" scope, and the definition of Services (1.8) already includes support and maintenance, so Vendor's operational ability to secure and support the Services is unaffected.

No additions, no boilerplate, no survival tail, no procedure and no extra remedy were inserted; the ownership, assignment, further-assurances, feedback, Affiliate-licence and contractor-support mechanics are all retained verbatim, so there is no duplicate operative coverage.

Intent preserved: the 14.3 cross-reference to "the perpetual licence in Section 13.2" still resolves, no defined term is orphaned (the 1.3 carve-out for anonymized telemetry is untouched, so Vendor keeps its non-Customer-Data telemetry rights), and no retained sentence contradicts the narrowed processing scope.

Note for the drafter (rationale only, no further redline needed): 14.2 vests ownership "subject to payment of the applicable Fees" and Fees is defined narrowly as the Implementation Fee (1.5); that is a definitional quirk elsewhere in the document and does not affect this element set.
